questions.prompt: Where can `var` (local variable type inference, Java 10+) be used?

options.text: Only on local variables with an initializer inside methods/blocks (and lambda params in Java 11+)
On class fields and method parameters

questions.prompt: What is the default access level when no modifier (`public`, `private`, `protected`) is written on a Java class or member?
Why is `StringBuilder` preferred over `String` `+` inside a loop?

options.text: `String` is immutable, so `+` in a loop allocates a new string copy each iteration ($O(n^2)$); `StringBuilder` appends in-place

questions.prompt: What does a Java 15+ text block (`""" ... """`) provide?

options.text: Multi-line string literals with automatic incidental-whitespace stripping and no `\n` escaping

questions.prompt: What does a modern Java 14+ `switch` expression (`var label = switch (day) { case MON, FRI -> "work"; default -> "other"; };`) avoid?

options.text: Accidental `case` fallthrough (arrow `->` arms never fall through and don't need `break`)

questions.prompt: What happens when you unbox a `null` `Integer` into a primitive `int` (`Integer x = null; int y = x;`)?
How does `ArrayList<Integer>` differ from `int[]`?

options.text: `ArrayList` resizes dynamically and works with generics/Collections API; `int[]` is fixed-length and stores primitives without boxing

questions.prompt: What does `Objects.requireNonNull(arg, "arg required")` do?

options.text: Throws `NullPointerException` with the message immediately if `arg == null`, otherwise returns `arg`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Java `enum`s. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Enums are full classes that can have fields, private constructors, and methods
Enums are implicitly `final` and type-safe singletons

questions.prompt: What does `arr.length` vs `str.length()` vs `list.size()` reflect in Java?

options.text: Arrays use field `.length`, `String` uses method `.length()`, and `Collection`s use method `.size()`

questions.prompt: What is `Integer.parseInt("42")` vs `Integer.valueOf("42")`?
What does `static` on a method (`public static int add(int a, int b)`) mean?

options.text: It belongs to the class itself rather than an instance and has no `this` reference

questions.prompt: What does `this(...)` inside a Java constructor do?

options.text: Delegates to another overloaded constructor in the *same* class (must be the first statement)

questions.prompt: What does `System.out.printf("%s: %d%n", name, count)` use `%n` for?

options.text: Platform-independent line separator (`\n` on Unix, `\r\n` on Windows)

questions.prompt: What does `map.getOrDefault(key, 0)` do on a `Map<String, Integer>`?

options.text: Returns the mapped value if `key` exists, or `0` without modifying `map`

questions.prompt: What happens in Java if a `switch` statement (classic colon `case 1:`) omits `break;`?

options.text: Execution falls through into the next `case` block

questions.prompt: What is method overloading in Java?

options.text: Having multiple methods in the same class with the same name and different parameter lists

questions.prompt: How are arguments passed to methods in Java?

options.text: Strictly by value for everything (for objects, the *reference value* is copied, not the object itself)
By reference for objects, by value for primitives

questions.prompt: Select all valid `for` / iteration forms in Java. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `for (var s in list)` (`in` is JS/Python/C#, Java uses `:`)

questions.prompt: What does `Math.addExact(a, b)` do that `a + b` does not?

options.text: Throws `ArithmeticException` on integer overflow instead of silently wrapping

questions.prompt: What does `"abc".isBlank()` (Java 11+) check vs `.isEmpty()`?

options.text: `.isBlank()` returns `true` for empty OR whitespace-only strings; `.isEmpty()` returns `true` only when `length() == 0`

questions.prompt: What does `List.of("a", "b", "c")` (Java 9+) return?
What does `import static java.lang.Math.*;` allow?

options.text: Calling static members like `max(a, b)` or `PI` without prefixing `Math.`

questions.prompt: What does `"a,b,".split(",")` return in Java by default?

options.text: `["a", "b"]` (strips trailing empty strings unless a negative limit like `.split(",", -1)` is passed)

questions.prompt: What does `char` represent in Java?

options.text: A 16-bit unsigned UTF-16 code unit (`0` to `65,535`)

questions.prompt: What does `instanceof` do in `if (obj instanceof String s)` (Java 16+)?

options.text: Checks if `obj` is a `String` (and non-null) and binds it to pattern variable `s` in one step

What is a package-private constructor often used for in utility classes like `java.lang.Math`?

options.text: A `private` constructor prevents instantiating a static-only utility class

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Java exceptions at a basic level. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Checked exceptions (subclasses of `Exception`, excluding `RuntimeException`) must be caught or declared with `throws`
Unchecked exceptions (`RuntimeException` subclasses like `IllegalArgumentException`) do not require `throws` declarations
`finally` always runs after `try`/`catch` (unless `System.exit` or JVM crash)
Catching `Throwable` or `Error` (like `OutOfMemoryError`) is recommended in normal business logic

questions.prompt: What does `Boolean.parseBoolean("TRUE")` return?

options.text: `true` (case-insensitive check for `"true"`, returning `false` for everything else)

questions.prompt: What does `>>>` (unsigned right shift) do in Java compared to `>>`?

options.text: `>>>` shifts in `0` bits at the sign bit (logical shift), whereas `>>` preserves the sign bit (arithmetic shift)

questions.prompt: What does `System.arraycopy` do?

options.text: Copies a range of elements between arrays natively at high speed (handling overlapping same-array copies safely)

questions.prompt: Select all valid `record` features in Java 16+. (Select all that apply.)

Generates `private final` fields, canonical constructor, accessor methods (`user.name()`), `equals`, `hashCode`, and `toString`

Records can implement `interface`s and define compact constructors for validation

questions.prompt: What does `"hello".formatted(args)` (Java 15+) or `String.format` do?

options.text: Formats a template string with `%s`/`%d` placeholders cleanly as an instance method
